questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: A student isolating DNA from plant leaves wants to break the cell wall and then free the DNA of RNA and proteins. Which combination of enzymes should be used?

options.text: Cellulase for the cell wall, ribonuclease for RNA and protease for proteins
Lysozyme for the cell wall, ribonuclease for RNA and protease for proteins
Chitinase for the cell wall, ribonuclease for RNA and protease for proteins
Cellulase for the cell wall, ribonuclease for proteins and protease for RNA

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem:
Arrange the following steps in the development of an insect-resistant transgenic plant in the correct order.
(A) Regeneration of whole plants from the transformed cells by tissue culture
(B) Insertion of the cry gene into the Ti plasmid
(C) Isolation of the cry gene from Bacillus thuringiensis
(D) Infection of plant explants with Agrobacterium carrying the recombinant plasmid

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: In the first commercial production of human insulin by recombinant DNA technology, the A and B polypeptide chains were made in separate E. coli cultures and then:

options.text: extracted and joined by creating disulphide bonds between them
joined end to end by peptide bonds formed by the enzyme DNA ligase
treated with enzymes to remove a C peptide from each chain
cut by restriction endonucleases and ligated into one plasmid

questions.stem: A foreign company is granted a patent on a product made from a crop variety that farmers of another country developed over centuries, without the farmers' permission or any compensation to them. This is an example of:

options.text: Bioprospecting
Biofortification
Bioethics
Biopiracy

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: Transgenic animals are preferred to normal animals for toxicity testing of chemicals because they:

options.text: grow and reproduce much faster, so many generations can be tested quickly
carry genes that make them more sensitive to toxic substances
have a faster metabolism, so the chemical is cleared from the body quickly
carry human genes that neutralise the chemical before it can harm them

questions.stem: The plate-based test described for the first patient is an example of:

options.text: Polymerase chain reaction assay
Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay
Gel electrophoresis of serum proteins
Radioactive probe hybridisation

questions.passage_text:
A hospital laboratory receives blood samples from two patients. The first patient has had a fever for several days. The laboratory coats the wells of a plastic plate with a protein from the suspected virus, adds the patient's serum and washes the plate. A second antibody carrying an enzyme is then added, followed by a colourless substrate. A well turns coloured only if the serum held antibodies that stuck to the viral protein, and a deeper colour means more antibody. Because antibodies appear in the blood only some days after infection, the laboratory uses another approach for people exposed very recently: a short stretch of the pathogen's genetic material is copied millions of times in a thermal cycler, so that even a tiny number of pathogen particles can be found.

The second sample is from a newborn who is being screened for an inherited disorder caused by a mutation in one gene. A short single-stranded DNA fragment, tagged with a radioactive label, is added to the baby's denatured DNA. The fragment is complementary to the normal sequence of the gene, and it attaches only where it finds that sequence. The places where it has attached are later shown by exposing a photographic film.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: A person exposed to the virus only a day earlier is tested by both the plate method and the copying method described. The most likely results, in that order, are:

options.text: antibodies detected; pathogen genetic material not detected
antibodies not detected; pathogen genetic material not detected
antibodies detected; pathogen genetic material detected
antibodies not detected; pathogen genetic material detected

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about the two tests described.
(A) The first test detects antibodies made against the viral protein, not the virus itself.
(B) The enzyme that produces the colour is carried by the second antibody.
(C) The labelled fragment used in the second test is double-stranded.
(D) The second test depends on base pairing between the fragment and the baby's DNA.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.

options.text: (A), (B) and (D) only
(A), (C) and (D) only
(B), (C) and (D) only
(A), (B) and (C) only

Consider the following statements about ecological pyramids.
(A) The pyramid of biomass in the sea is generally inverted.

(B), (C) and (D) only

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: Which of the following statements about the species-area relationship is correct?

options.text: Plotted on log scales it is a straight line whose slope is steepest for very large areas such as entire continents
Plotted on arithmetic scales it is a straight line whose slope is the same for all taxonomic groups and regions
Within a region, species richness keeps rising in proportion to the area explored, with no upper limit
The slope on log scales is 0.6 to 1.2 for small areas and 0.1 to 0.2 for entire continents

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a reason suggested for the greater species diversity of the tropics compared with temperate regions?

Tropical regions were repeatedly covered by glaciers, which forced their species to diversify rapidly
Tropical environments are less seasonal and more constant, which promotes niche specialisation
Greater solar energy in the tropics gives higher productivity, which supports more species

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a broadly utilitarian argument for conserving biodiversity?

options.text: Forest plants yield timber, resin and medicines that can be sold

Pollinators in a forest raise the yield of crops on nearby farms
Wild relatives of crops are screened for new drugs and industrial products
